question.text: Who does DMV vision-test, and why?

answer.text: DMV vision-tests every applicant to confirm sight adequate for safe driving.

teaching.text: No one skips the vision test; DMV checks every applicant's sight for safe driving. Remember: everyone's eyes get checked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: DMV vision-tests every applicant to confirm sight adequate for safe driving.

question.text: What happens to your license if you take the vision test wearing glasses or contacts?

answer.text: Testing while wearing corrective or contact lenses puts a corrective lenses restriction on the license.

teaching.text: Pass the vision test in your glasses or contacts and your license will note that you need them. Remember: lenses on, restriction on.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Testing while wearing corrective or contact lenses puts a corrective lenses restriction on the license.

question.text: Where does a failed vision test send you, and for what form?

answer.text: A failed vision test sends you to an eye doctor for a completed Report of Vision Examination (DL sixty-two) form.

teaching.text: Not passing the vision test means a visit to an eye doctor, who completes the Report of Vision Examination form. Remember: fail it, see the eye doctor.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A failed vision test sends you to an eye doctor for a completed Report of Vision Examination (DL sixty-two) form.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: fail it, see the eye doctor

question.text: Where are the vision standards detailed?

answer.text: Vision standards detail lives at dmv.ca.gov slash vision-standards.

teaching.text: The full vision standards are spelled out on the DMV vision standards page. Remember: vision standards page.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vision standards detail lives at dmv.ca.gov slash vision-standards.

question.text: What kind of knowledge test does an original license require?

answer.text: An original license requires passing a knowledge test built from multiple choice questions.

teaching.text: For an original license, the knowledge test is made of multiple choice questions on the handbook. Remember: multiple choice for originals.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An original license requires passing a knowledge test built from multiple choice questions.

question.text: How many attempts do you get at the knowledge test before you must reapply?

answer.text: You get three attempts to pass before you must reapply.

teaching.text: Three tries is the limit; after that you start over with a new application. Remember: three tries, then reapply.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You get three attempts to pass before you must reapply.

question.text: How long must a minor wait to retake a failed knowledge test?

answer.text: Minors wait seven days, excluding the failure day, before retaking a failed knowledge test.

teaching.text: A minor who fails the knowledge test waits seven days, and the failure day itself does not count. Remember: seven days for knowledge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Minors wait seven days, excluding the failure day, before retaking a failed knowledge test.

question.text: What may renewing drivers take instead of the knowledge test, and how does it work?

answer.text: Renewals may substitute eLearning, a no-fail self-paced interactive modulated course with quizzes after each module, taken on computer, laptop, tablet, or mobile device.

teaching.text: At renewal you may take eLearning instead: a self-paced, no-fail course with a quiz after each module, on any device. Remember: renewals can eLearn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Renewals may substitute eLearning, a no-fail self-paced interactive modulated course with quizzes after each module, taken on computer, laptop, tablet, or mobile device.

question.text: When do testing options open up?

answer.text: Testing options open up once the application at dmv.ca.gov slash dl is complete.

teaching.text: Finish your application on the DMV license page first, and then your testing options open. Remember: apply first, then test.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Testing options open up once the application at dmv.ca.gov slash dl is complete.

question.text: Which testing aids may you use during a knowledge test?

answer.text: No testing aids are allowed during knowledge tests, neither the handbook nor a cell phone.

teaching.text: Leave the handbook and your phone aside; no testing aids are allowed during the knowledge test. Remember: no book, no phone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No testing aids are allowed during knowledge tests, neither the handbook nor a cell phone.

question.text: What are the format, attempts and minor retake wait of the knowledge test?

answer.text: The knowledge test bundles format, attempts, and retakes: multiple choice questions, three tries before reapplying, and a seven-day minor wait excluding the failure day.

teaching.text: For the knowledge test, remember the bundle: multiple choice, three tries, and a seven-day wait for minors. Remember: choices, three tries, seven days.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The knowledge test bundles format, attempts, and retakes: multiple choice questions, three tries before reapplying, and a seven-day minor wait excluding the failure day.

question.text: Who may use eLearning, and what can it never replace?

answer.text: eLearning is the renewal-only no-fail self-paced course with quizzes per module, never a substitute for the original-license knowledge test.

teaching.text: eLearning helps only at renewal and never takes the place of the first knowledge test. Remember: renewal only course.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: eLearning is the renewal-only no-fail self-paced course with quizzes per module, never a substitute for the original-license knowledge test.

question.text: Who must take a behind-the-wheel test?

answer.text: Original applicants take a behind-the-wheel test of safe driving ability, and renewing drivers with a vision or medical condition may have to take one too.

teaching.text: Every original applicant takes the drive test, and a vision or medical condition can bring a renewing driver back for one. Remember: originals drive, some renewals too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Original applicants take a behind-the-wheel test of safe driving ability, and renewing drivers with a vision or medical condition may have to take one too.

question.text: Why might the examiner give two or more instructions at once?

answer.text: The examiner may stack two or more instructions at once to see whether you grasp and follow both.

teaching.text: Expect the examiner to give more than one instruction at a time to see if you follow each one. Remember: listen for stacked instructions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The examiner may stack two or more instructions at once to see whether you grasp and follow both.

question.text: Where do you book a drive test appointment?

answer.text: Drive-test appointments are booked at dmv.ca.gov slash make-an-appointment.

teaching.text: Drive-test appointments are made on the DMV make-an-appointment page. Remember: book online.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drive-test appointments are booked at dmv.ca.gov slash make-an-appointment.

question.text: How long must a minor wait to retake a failed behind-the-wheel test?

answer.text: Minors wait fourteen days, excluding the failure day, before retaking a failed behind-the-wheel test.

teaching.text: A minor who fails the drive test waits fourteen days, not counting the day of the failure. Remember: fourteen days for driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Minors wait fourteen days, excluding the failure day, before retaking a failed behind-the-wheel test.

question.text: What does each of the three tests check?

answer.text: Three tests gate three things: vision screens eyesight, knowledge probes rules, and the drive test grades real skill.

teaching.text: Each test has one job: eyesight for vision, rules for knowledge, and driving skill for the drive test. Remember: eyes, rules, skill.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Three tests gate three things: vision screens eyesight, knowledge probes rules, and the drive test grades real skill.

question.text: Which document of your own should you bring on test day?

answer.text: On test day bring the instruction permit or license if one exists.

teaching.text: If you already hold a permit or license, bring it with you on test day. Remember: bring your permit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On test day bring the instruction permit or license if one exists.

question.text: Who must come with you on test day if you are not already licensed?

answer.text: Also bring another California-licensed driver aged at least eighteen, twenty-five for minors, unless already licensed to drive.

teaching.text: Unless you are already licensed, bring a licensed driver at least eighteen, or at least twenty-five if you are a minor. Remember: bring a licensed adult.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Also bring another California-licensed driver aged at least eighteen, twenty-five for minors, unless already licensed to drive.

question.text: What must the test vehicle and its papers include?

answer.text: Bring a vehicle safe for the test plus valid insurance proof and vehicle registration.

teaching.text: The car you test in must be safe and come with valid insurance proof and its registration. Remember: safe car, insured, registered.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bring a vehicle safe for the test plus valid insurance proof and vehicle registration.

question.text: When may a rental car be used for the drive test?

answer.text: Rental cars qualify only with your name on the rental contract and no contract clause excluding drive tests.

teaching.text: A rental car works only if your name is on the contract and the contract does not exclude drive tests. Remember: your name on the rental.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rental cars qualify only with your name on the rental contract and no contract clause excluding drive tests.

question.text: What four categories must you bring on test day?

answer.text: Test day needs four bring-categories: papers for you, a licensed adult beside you, a legal car beneath you, and rental terms that permit testing.

teaching.text: Test day takes four things: your papers, a licensed adult, a legal car, and rental terms that allow testing. Remember: papers, adult, car, contract.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Test day needs four bring-categories: papers for you, a licensed adult beside you, a legal car beneath you, and rental terms that permit testing.

question.text: What does the pre-drive check start with?

answer.text: The pre-drive check starts with an opening driver window and a windshield giving you and the examiner a full, clear, unblocked view, since cracks can postpone the test.

teaching.text: The check starts at the driver window, which must open, and a windshield with a full clear view; cracks can delay the test. Remember: window opens, view clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The pre-drive check starts with an opening driver window and a windshield giving you and the examiner a full, clear, unblocked view, since cracks can postpone the test.

question.text: How many rearview mirrors must the test vehicle have, and where?

answer.text: At least two rearview mirrors are required, with one on the vehicle's left side.

teaching.text: Count the mirrors: at least two, and one has to be on the left side of the vehicle. Remember: two mirrors, one left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At least two rearview mirrors are required, with one on the vehicle's left side.

question.text: Which brake lights must work on the test vehicle?

answer.text: Both right and left brake lights must work.

teaching.text: Both brake lights, right and left, have to light up. Remember: both brake lights glow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Both right and left brake lights must work.

question.text: What tread depth must the tires have, and which spare is barred?

answer.text: Tires need at least one thirty-second-inch of uniformed tread depth, and donut tires are barred from the test.

teaching.text: Tires need a minimum of tread, a thirty-second of an inch, and a donut spare is not allowed on the test. Remember: tread deep enough, no donut.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tires need at least one thirty-second-inch of uniformed tread depth, and donut tires are barred from the test.

question.text: How much clearance must the pressed foot brake keep above the floorboard?

answer.text: The depressed foot brake must keep at least one inch of clearance above the floorboard.

teaching.text: Press the foot brake down and at least one inch should remain between the pedal and the floor. Remember: an inch above the floor.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The depressed foot brake must keep at least one inch of clearance above the floorboard.

question.text: What must be true of the test vehicle's horn?

answer.text: The horn must be vehicle-designed, working, and audible from at least two hundred feet away.

teaching.text: The horn has to be the vehicle's own, it has to work, and it has to be heard from two hundred feet. Remember: horn heard far away.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The horn must be vehicle-designed, working, and audible from at least two hundred feet away.

question.text: Which numbers must the test vehicle meet?

answer.text: The car's numbers cluster: at least two mirrors with one left, thirty-second-inch tread minimum, one inch of pedal clearance, and a horn heard at two hundred feet.

teaching.text: The numbers to know: two mirrors, a thirty-second of an inch of tread, one inch of pedal clearance, and a horn heard at two hundred feet. Remember: mirrors, tread, pedal, horn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The car's numbers cluster: at least two mirrors with one left, thirty-second-inch tread minimum, one inch of pedal clearance, and a horn heard at two hundred feet.

question.text: What must you show about the parking brake?

answer.text: You must show how to set and release the parking brake.

teaching.text: Be ready to set the parking brake and then release it for the examiner. Remember: set it, release it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must show how to set and release the parking brake.

question.text: Which arm signals must you demonstrate?

answer.text: You must demonstrate the left turn, right turn, and slowing-or-stopping arm signals.

teaching.text: Practice all three arm signals: left turn, right turn, and slowing or stopping. Remember: left, right, slow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must demonstrate the left turn, right turn, and slowing-or-stopping arm signals.

question.text: What happens with the wipers and seat belts during the check?

answer.text: Wipers may be function-checked, and every seat belt must work and be worn by each occupant.

teaching.text: The examiner may test the wipers, and every person in the car must wear a working seat belt. Remember: every belt buckled.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wipers may be function-checked, and every seat belt must work and be worn by each occupant.

question.text: What three demonstrations does the vehicle check ask for?

answer.text: The demo trio is hands, arms, and gear: set and release the parking brake, flash all three arm signals, and prove wipers plus belts.

teaching.text: You show three things: the parking brake, the three arm signals, and working wipers and belts. Remember: brake, signals, wipers and belts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The demo trio is hands, arms, and gear: set and release the parking brake, flash all three arm signals, and prove wipers plus belts.

question.text: What happens if the vehicle fails the requirements?

answer.text: A vehicle that fails these requirements gets the drive test rescheduled.

teaching.text: If the car does not meet the requirements, the drive test is moved to another day. Remember: bad car, new date.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle that fails these requirements gets the drive test rescheduled.

question.text: How far may an interpreter help during the drive test?

answer.text: Interpreters may help identify and use controls in the pre-drive inspection but cannot ride along for the test.

teaching.text: An interpreter can help you find and use controls during the inspection, but stays out of the car for the drive. Remember: interpreter stays outside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Interpreters may help identify and use controls in the pre-drive inspection but cannot ride along for the test.

question.text: Who may ride along on the drive test?

answer.text: Only the examiner accompanies the drive test, except for training, service animals, and certain law enforcement situations.

teaching.text: Apart from training, service animals, and some law enforcement cases, only the examiner rides with you. Remember: just you and the examiner.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only the examiner accompanies the drive test, except for training, service animals, and certain law enforcement situations.

question.text: What is the rule on recording devices during the drive test?

answer.text: Recording devices, including video recorders, are prohibited on the drive test, and one that cannot power off must be blocked from all visual and audio recording.

teaching.text: Switch off any recording device, and block any that cannot be switched off from capturing video or sound. Remember: no recording at all.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Recording devices, including video recorders, are prohibited on the drive test, and one that cannot power off must be blocked from all visual and audio recording.

question.text: What are the limits on riders, interpreters and recorders during the drive test?

answer.text: Only the examiner rides along, interpreters stop at the pre-drive inspection, and every recorder stays off or blocked.

teaching.text: The examiner rides alone with you, interpreters help only before the drive, and recorders stay off. Remember: examiner only, recorders off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only the examiner rides along, interpreters stop at the pre-drive inspection, and every recorder stays off or blocked.

question.text: Which kind of vehicle technology is banned on the drive test, and why?

answer.text: Because the test grades the driver rather than the car, assistance tech such as automated parallel parking, lane departure, and adaptive cruise control is banned.

teaching.text: Features that do the driving, like automated parking, lane departure help, or adaptive cruise control, are banned on the test. Remember: the test grades you.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Because the test grades the driver rather than the car, assistance tech such as automated parallel parking, lane departure, and adaptive cruise control is banned.

question.text: Which vehicle safety technology is allowed, and what must you still do?

answer.text: Safety tech such as backup cameras and blind spot monitors is allowed yet never replaces direct mirror and blind-spot checks.

teaching.text: Backup cameras and blind spot monitors may stay on, but you must still check mirrors and blind spots yourself. Remember: cameras help, eyes still check.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Safety tech such as backup cameras and blind spot monitors is allowed yet never replaces direct mirror and blind-spot checks.

question.text: How does banned assistance technology differ from allowed safety technology?

answer.text: Assistance tech that drives for you is banned, while safety tech that only shows you more is allowed yet never replaces your own eyes.

teaching.text: Tech that drives for you is out; tech that only helps you see is in, but your own eyes still do the checking. Remember: helpers banned, viewers allowed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Assistance tech that drives for you is banned, while safety tech that only shows you more is allowed yet never replaces your own eyes.

question.text: Where can you find sample Driving Performance Evaluation Score Sheets?

answer.text: Sample Driving Performance Evaluation Score Sheets live at dmv.ca.gov slash teendriver, with Supplemental and Area sheets at dmv.ca.gov slash seniors.

teaching.text: Sample drive test score sheets are posted on the DMV teen driver page, with supplemental and area sheets on the seniors page. Remember: sample sheets online.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Sample Driving Performance Evaluation Score Sheets live at dmv.ca.gov slash teendriver, with Supplemental and Area sheets at dmv.ca.gov slash seniors.
